questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among $Ce   \left(4f^{1}5d^{1}6s^{2}\right), Nd  \left(4f^{1}6s^{2}\right), $Eu $\left(4f^{7}6s^{2}\right)$ and Dy$\left(4f^{10}6s^{2}\right), the elements having highest and lowest $3$rd& ionisation energies, respectively are$
questions.solution:
For& $3rd$ ionisation energy, the electron must be removed from~$+ 2$ oxidation state of given metals. The electronic configuration of~$Ce$ is

$4f^{1}5d^{1}6s^{2}$

The electronic configuration of ${Ce}^{2 +}$ is

$4f^{1}5d^{1}$

The electronic configuration of $Nd$ is

$4f^{4}6s^{2}$

The electronic configuration of ${Nd}^{2 +}$ is

$4f^{4}$

The electronic configuration of~$Eu$ is

$4f^{7}6s^{2}$

The electronic configuration of ${Eu}^{2 +}$ is

$4f^{7}$

The electronic configuration of $Dy$~is

$4f^{10}6s^{2}$

The electronic configuration of ${Dy}^{2 +}$ is $4f^{10}$~$Eu$~will have the maximum $3rd$~ionisation enthalphy, because the electron has to be removed from stable half-filled $\left(4f^{7}\right){Eu}^{2 +}$ configuration, whereas $Ce$~will have the lowest $3rd$~ionisation enthalpy as the electron has to be removed from $5d$-orbital.
